August 3, 1932.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL）
POLICE FORCE.
COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE.
P. O. Box No. 158
Commissioner of Police,
Sir,
Mr. Burgoyne has been interviewed and told
that the Police must have an opportunity of perusing
books intended for sale in the Settlement before they
can pass an opinion as to whether the sale of these books
is advisable or not, and a suggestion has been made to
him that H. M's Commercial Counsellor will probably
be able to give the advice he is seeking.
There is a fairly extensive trade done in
Shanghai in books which obviously emanate from Soviet
sources.
In view of the above I suggest that it will
not be necessary to send a written reply to Mr. Burgoyne's
letter of July 16.
（批：M G 3/8）
（签名）
Officer i/c Special Branch.

伯戈因（Burgoyne）先生已接受问询，并被告知，警方必须有机会审阅拟在租界内销售的书籍，方能就销售这些书籍是否适宜发表意见；同时已向他建议，英国陛下政府商务参赞或许能够提供他所寻求的建议。

Subject (in full)........................................Kwaung Hsueh Publishing Company.

Made by......D.S. Moore.......................Forwarded by......[签名]

The attached file on E.J. Burgoyne and the Kwang
Hsueh Publishing Co. has been shown to the official designated
by the Officer i/c Special Branch on the attached memo.
It is his considered unofficial opinion that any contract
entered into by the Kwang Hsueh Publishing Co. with J.A. Brown
of Harbin is so obviously likly to be abused by the principals
in whose interests the latter is acting, that the good name of
the Kwang Hsueh Publishing Co. and E.J. Burgoyne will be
prejudiced and that therefore, Burgoyne should be advised to
drop the negotiations at their present stage.

（批：JB）

DSB Moore

REPORT
Special Branch B. 228/329
Date July 24, 1932

Subject (in full) Attached Letter re Soviet Russian Literature.

Made by D.S. Moore. Forwarded by [签名]

Regarding the attached letter from the Kwang Hsueh
Publishing House ( 廣學書局 ) over the signature of Mr. E.J.
Burgoyne, seeking an opinion as to the advisability or otherwise
of accepting the local agency for the sale of literature exported
from Soviet Russia.
E.J. Burgoyne is the general manager of the Anglo-French
Press, 41-43 Avenue Edward VII and also acts in an executive
capacity for the Kwang Hsueh Publishing House, 44 Peking Road,
a concern dealing in religious and educational books. The
former prints the books required by the latter.
Some little while ago the brother of E.J. Burgoyne, who
is also engaged in the same printing business, was in Harbin
and there met one J.A. Brown, a British subject, who is well
known to both of the brothers Burgoyne. Brown who has a
Russian wife and who gives his address in Harbin as "Bookselling
Department, 35 Yamskaya Street, Harbin, Manchuria, P.O. Box 289"
is the agent in that city of Messrs Mustard and Co. and also
representative of the Swedish Match Trust. Previous to obtaining
employment in Harbin he was engaged for many years in furthering
the interests of the British American Tobacco Co. in various
parts of Manchuria. As an outcome of the meeting in Harbin
between Burgoyne and Brown, negotiations were begun for the
opening of a local agency for the distribution of Russian
literature in Shanghai. This was followed by a visit to
Shanghai of one F.M. Basov, a Russian subject working under
Brown in Harbin. The proposal was then advanced that there
should be a reciprocation of trade between the two houses
concerned, that is, English books should be sent to Harbin in
exchange for Russian books shipped to Shanghai. Basov who re-

事由（全称）：关于苏联俄罗斯文学的附信。

制作人：D.S. Moore。转呈人：[签名]

关于广学书局（廣學書局）E.J. Burgoyne 先生署名的附信，该局就接受代理销售从苏联俄罗斯出口的文学作品是否适宜一事征询意见。
E.J. Burgoyne 是位于爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）41-43号的英法印刷所（Anglo-French Press）总经理，同时也以执行人员身份任职于北京路44号的广学书局，这是一家经营宗教和教育书籍的商号。前者印制后者所需的书籍。
不久前，E.J. Burgoyne 的兄弟也从事同一印刷业务，他在哈尔滨期间结识了 J.A. Brown，此人为英国臣民，为 Burgoyne 兄弟二人所熟知。Brown 娶有一位俄罗斯妻子，其在哈尔滨的地址为“中国满洲哈尔滨亚姆斯卡亚街（Yamskaya Street）35号售书部，邮政信箱289号”，他是 Mustard 公司在该市的代理人，同时也是瑞典火柴托拉斯的代表。在受雇于哈尔滨之前，他曾在满洲各地多年致力于促进英美烟草公司（British American Tobacco Co.）的利益。作为 Burgoyne 与 Brown 在哈尔滨会面的结果，双方开始就在上海开设代理处以分销俄罗斯文学进行谈判。随后，一名在哈尔滨受雇于 Brown 的俄罗斯籍人士 F.M. Basov 访问了上海。当时提出的建议是，两家相关商号之间应进行贸易互惠，即向哈尔滨发送英文书籍，以交换运往上海的俄罗斯书籍。Basov 重新……

sided at the Kavkaz Hotel, 971 Bubbling Well Road during his
sojourn in this city, presented the Kwang Hsueh Publishing
House with a draft agreement during one of his visits to that
concern. The most striking feature of this phase in the
negotiations is that the draft agreement is in the Russian
language, which neither of the Burgoyne's are conversant with.
During an interview with the undersigned, Mr. E.J.
Burgoyne remarked on the strangeness of the fact that the draft
agreement is in Russian and stated that he has been given to
understand all books exported from the U.S.S.R. have first to
be passed by the Soviet Censor and further if he accepts the
proposal as outlined above he will confine himself to dealing in
Medical, Educational and works of General Literature.
Edgar John Burgoyne is an Australian and is about
50 years of age. Both he and his brother, A.E.L. Burgoyne have
been in the Far East for several years and were for some time
advertising agents and travellers for the British American
Tobacco Co., in Manchuria. Since then they have been concerned
in various business enterprises in Shanghai and both are
described as industrious, of quiet habits and very attentive
to business.
Attached is a translation of the draft agreement sent
to E.J. Burgoyne by A.J. Brown [████████████████████████████]ame.

在沪逗留期间下榻于静安寺路971号高加索旅馆（Kavkaz Hotel），并在一次拜访该商号时，向广学书局提交了一份协议草案。此阶段谈判中最引人注目的特点是，该协议草案系用俄文写成，而伯戈因（Burgoyne）兄弟二人均不通晓俄语。在与卑职面谈时，E.J. 伯戈因先生对协议草案为俄文这一奇怪事实发表了评论，并表示他获悉，所有从苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟出口的书籍均须先经苏联审查机关通过；此外，如果他接受上述提议，他将仅限于经营医学、教育及一般文学类书籍。
埃德加·约翰·伯戈因（Edgar John Burgoyne）系澳大利亚人，年约五十岁。他与其兄 A.E.L. 伯戈因已在远东居住数年，并曾在满洲担任英美烟草公司的广告代理人和推销员。此后，他们参与了在上海的各项商业企业，两人均被描述为勤奋、习性安静且非常专注于业务。
随函附上 A.J. 布朗 [███…]ame 发送给 E.J. 伯戈因的协议草案译文。

J.R

W.B. 穆尔。
D. S.

Translation from Russian

AGREEMENT

"July 1932, British subject J.A. Brown, further
called the vendor and Kwang Hsueh Publishing House,
further called the Buyer entered into a contract on the
following terms :-

(1) The Vendor makes over the right of representation
and sale to Buyer in Shanghai, Tientsin, Peking and other
towns of South China, of printed productions of USSR,
i.e. books, manuals, school-books, antiquarian and pre-
war editions, music, etc. allowed for sale by local
police and censorship regulations, for the term of one
year from the 1st of August 1932 to the 1st of August
1933 and the patent right of sale of the mentioned
goods in the indicated area, which right was obtained
by the Vendor by an agreement from the "Centrosojus"
in Shanghai on " " June 1932.

(2) Books are delivered at nominal prices with the
following discount from their value :-
a) Books referring to statistical literature -
with discount of 35%.
b) All other books a discount of 30%. When not
less than ten copies of the same publication
are simultaneously ordered, except school-books,
one copy (the tenth) is delivered gratis.
c) Subscribed editions (encyclopedia, inquiries, etc.)
are delivered with a discount of 15%.
d) Papers and magazines - with a discount of 20%.
e) Music - with discount of 35 %.
Remark Prices are understood franco Shanghai.
In all cases when books are received by the Buyer
direct from Moscow, and in cases of delivery of
goods to the Buyer from Harbin the cost of delivery
from Harbin to Shanghai will be charged to the
Buyer's account. Custom duty and other taxes
are all charged to the Buyer's account.
f) Antiquarian and pre-war editions are delivered
with a discount of 15% from the price lists, with
all expenses for delivery duty and taxes charged
to the Buyer's account.
Remark No discount is allowed from the price of
bindings and their cost is charged to the Buyer's
account.

(3) The Buyer engages to order and redeem the goods
mentioned in Item 1 for one year for the sum of not less
than six thousand ($6,000) American Dollars, calculated on
the nominal prices and between the following dates :-
From August 1, 1932 to November 1932 for $1,000
From November 1, 1932 to February 1, 1933 for $2,500.
From February 1, 1933 to May 1, 1933 for $1,500, and
From May 1, 1933 to August 1, 1933 for $1,000.

(4) Calculations for the goods and also for all the
expenses are charged to the Buyer's account in American
Gold Dollars at the current rate - one rouble for fifty
American cents.

(5) Calculations are made in the following way :-
a) 50% of the cost of the delivered goods are to be
paid for by the Buyer against the goods and
reckoning of the Vendor in Shanghai to the

俄文译文

协议

“1932年7月，英国臣民 J.A. Brown（以下简称‘卖方’）与广学书局（Kwang Hsueh Publishing House，以下简称‘买方’）订立合同，条款如下：-

(1) 卖方将苏联印刷品（即书籍、手册、教科书、古籍及战前版本、乐谱等）在上海、天津、北平及华南其他城镇的代表权和销售权转让给买方，前提是上述物品符合当地警察及审查法规允许销售的规定。转让期限为一年，自1932年8月1日起至1933年8月1日止；同时转让在上述指定区域内销售上述货物的专利销售权，该权利系卖方于1932年6月__日通过与上海‘Centrosojus’（音译）签订的协议获得。

(2) 书籍按名义价格交付，并按其价值给予以下折扣：-
a) 统计类文献书籍 - 折扣35%。
b) 所有其他书籍 - 折扣30%。若同时订购同一出版物不少于十册（教科书除外），则其中一册（即第十册）免费赠送。
c) 订阅版出版物（百科全书、查询工具书等） - 折扣15%。
d) 报纸和杂志 - 折扣20%。
e) 乐谱 - 折扣35%。
备注：价格理解为上海离岸价（franco Shanghai）。在所有由买方直接从莫斯科接收书籍的情况下，以及在货物从哈尔滨交付给买方的情况下，从哈尔滨到上海的运输费用将记入买方账户。关税及其他税费均记入买方账户。
f) 古籍及战前版本按价目表价格给予15%的折扣交付，所有运输、关税及税费均由买方承担。
备注：装订费不予折扣，其费用由买方承担。

(3) 买方承诺在一年内订购并赎买第1款所述货物，总金额按名义价格计算不少于六千（$6,000）美元，并在以下日期区间内完成：-
1932年8月1日至1932年11月，金额为1,000美元
1932年11月1日至1933年2月1日，金额为2,500美元。
1933年2月1日至1933年5月1日，金额为1,500美元，以及
1933年5月1日至1933年8月1日，金额为1,000美元。

(4) 货款及所有费用的结算均以美国金元按现行汇率记入买方账户——即1卢布兑50美分。

(5) 结算方式如下：-
a) 已交付货物成本的50%由买方凭货物及卖方在上海向

page_data.en:
(2)

"Centrosojus" in the account of the Vendor.
b) The remaining of 75% of the cost of the goods is to be paid by the Buyer to the Vendor not later than three months from the day of receipt of the goods, by sending the money to Harbin with the unfailing condition that the total debt of the Buyer does not exceed six Hundred (600) American Dollars.
Remarks The cost of sending money to Harbin is charged also to the Buyer's account.
c) Calculations for papers and magazines are to be made every month by payment by the Buyer to the Vendor of all sums received minus discount. The money is to be paid each time to the account of the Vendor in the "Centrosojus" at Shanghai.

(6) When the total debt of the Buyer has reached the sum of G$600 the Buyer will be obliged to pay cash for all goods received. The Vendor has the right to stop sending goods to the credit if the Buyer has not paid for them at due time and in this case the Buyer will be obliged to redeem all the goods for cash even if his debt by the previous allowed credit is less than G$500.

(7) Orders of the Buyer are carried out by the Vendor by sending goods from Moscow or other parts of USSR, on the instructions of the Buyer, as cargo, by post or in postal wrappers from the address of the Vendor or from any other address given by his instructions. All expenses covering Customs, postal, railway, censor, and other formalities and requests are all charged to the Buyer's account.

(8) If the Vendor for any reason is unable to carry out the orders he receives, he, the Vendor, is not responsible to the Buyer and the latter has no right of claim against him, neither has he any right of claim if the goods are lost or damaged whilst en route. If the goods as ordered arrive in Shanghai after two months from the receipt of the order or even before, but in a spoiled and damaged condition, the Buyer has a right to refuse to redeem the goods at a fixed price and in case of this refusal, the goods, late or damaged, are to be taken by the Buyer on commission without obligations on the part of the Buyer for the delay of or damaged to the said goods.
Remarks The value of orders received by the Vendor and not carried out by him, are included in the sum of the minimum circulation pointed out in Item 2 of this agreement, but in case the orders, received from the Buyer by the Vendor, are not executed for the reason that the ordered editions are not published in USSR or are all sold out, their value has no influence on the minimum circulation pointed out in Item 1 and is not included in this circulation.

(9) Goods which have been despatched must be redeemed by the Buyer in the order shown in Item 5, in each case not later than ten (10) days after the date of notification of the Buyer by the Vendor.

(10) If during the period fixed in Item 9 the Buyer does not redeem goods which have arrived in Shanghai, the Vendor has the right to realize the goods as his own property and the Buyer in this case is obliged to pay the Vendor a forfeit for the
page_data.zh:
(2)

‘Centrosojus’（音译）出具的卖方账户账单进行支付。
b) 剩余75%的货物成本由买方在收到货物之日起不超过三个月内支付给卖方，款项需汇往哈尔滨，前提条件是买方的总债务不超过六百（600）美元。
备注：汇款至哈尔滨的费用亦由买方承担。
c) 报纸和杂志的结算每月进行一次，由买方向卖方支付收到的全部款项减去折扣后的金额。每次付款均需汇入卖方在上海‘Centrosojus’（音译）的账户。

(6) 当买方总债务达到600金元时，买方须以现金支付所有收到的货物。若买方未按时付款，卖方有权停止赊销发货；在此情况下，即使买方此前的赊销债务低于500金元，也须以现金赎买所有货物。

(7) 卖方可根据买方指示，通过货运、邮政或邮政包裹形式，从莫斯科或苏联其他地区发送货物来履行买方订单，发件地址可为卖方地址或其指示的其他任何地址。所有涉及海关、邮政、铁路、审查及其他手续和要求的费用均记入买方账户。

(8) 若卖方因任何原因无法执行所接订单，卖方不对买方承担责任，买方亦无权向其提出索赔；若货物在运输途中丢失或损坏，买方同样无权提出索赔。若所订货物在收到订单两个月后（或甚至在此之前）抵达上海，但处于变质或损坏状态，买方有权拒绝按固定价格赎买货物；若买方拒绝，迟到或损坏的货物将由买方以代销方式接收，买方对此不承担任何关于延迟或损坏的责任。
备注：卖方收到但未执行的订单价值，计入本协议第2款所指的最小流通额中；但若卖方收到买方订单后因所订版本在苏联未出版或已售罄而未执行，其价值不影响第1款所指的最小流通额，也不计入该流通额中。

(9) 已发运的货物必须由买方按照第5款所示顺序赎买，且在每种情况下，不得晚于卖方通知买方之日后的十（10）天。

(10) 若在第9款规定的期限内，买方未赎买已抵达上海的货物，卖方有权将该货物作为其自有财产进行处置，在此情况下，买方须向卖方支付违约金，以补偿

(3)

breach of contract in the sum of 10% of the value of the
goods not redeemed.

(11) Payment for goods delivered on a commission basis
must be made every four (4) months, by the dispatch by the
Buyer to the Vendor at Harbin of the necessary sums. The
value of goods sold on a commission basis is entered in the
sum of the minimum circulation by this agreement. If
during six months from the date of receipt of goods delivered
on a commission basis, the goods are not returned to the
Vendor, the goods will be regarded as sold to the Buyer at
a fixed price and he will be obliged to pay for them at
once. The Buyer cannot request from the Vendor any expenses
incurred through the storage or return of unsold commission
basis goods.

(12) The Vendor will not be responsible of the goods
mentioned in Item 1 are sold in Shanghai and the other
places mentioned in this agreement, by persons other than
the Buyer.

(13) The Buyer has the right to return a proportionate
amount of the goods delivered to him, namely :- (a) from
unsold books - (novels, understood books of the first
edition) ordered by the Buyer and when the names of the
books were not mentioned, the Buyer has the right during the
first four months from the date of receipt of the goods, to
return to the Vendor books to the value of 25% of the
original order. When one copy of a book is ordered as a
sample, the Buyer has the right to return it to the Vendor,
but must do so not later than four months from the day of
receipt. (b) From other books (except pre-war, antiquarian
and subscription editions) the Buyer has the right to return
to the Vendor any books not sold during six (6) months from
the date of their receipt, up to 10% of the nominal cost of
the said books. All books returned by the Buyer must be
in good order, clean and with pages intact. All expenses
incurred in sending goods back to Harbin or where indicated
by the Vendor, will be charged to the account of the Buyer.

(14) In case the Nominal value of goods not redeemed by
the Buyer at various times reaches the value of G$300 or
if the Buyer does not make payment in due time or during the
first three-quarters does not redeem goods to the value of
G$5,000, the Vendor has the right by his unilateral order
to discontinue this agreement and the Buyer has no claim
on the Vendor.

(15) If during one year i.e. until August 1, 1933, the
Buyer does not purchase from the Vendor, goods as named in
Item 1 to the value of G$5,000, the Buyer will be obliged
to, not later than 20 days i.e. August 20, 1933 to pay the
Vendor an infraction of 10% of the sum, making the circulation
less than G$5,000. If the failure of the circulation will
be above G$1,000 he will be obliged to pay infraction of
20% and not 10%.

(16) As a guarantee of the fulfillment by the Buyer of
his obligations according to this agreement, he will sign
this agreement and produce for the satisfaction of the
Vendor a guarantee from a foreign bank for the sum of
G$500 (term December 25, 1933) and a letter of exchange for
the sum of G$400, the same to be exchanged in half a year.
page_data.zh:
(3)

违约赔偿金为未赎回货物价值的 10%。

(11) 委托代销货物的货款必须每四（4）个月支付一次，由买方将必要款项汇寄给位于哈尔滨的卖方。根据本协议，委托代销货物的价值计入最低流通额。如果在收到委托代销货物之日起六个月内，货物未退还给卖方，则该等货物将被视为已按固定价格出售给买方，买方须立即付款。买方不得就未售出的委托代销货物的仓储或退货运费向卖方索取任何费用。

(12) 如果第 1 项所述货物在上海及本协议提及的其他地方被买方以外的人销售，卖方对此不承担任何责任。

(13) 买方有权退回向其交付的部分货物，即：(a) 对于买方订购的未售出书籍（小说，理解为初版书），且在订单中未列明书名的情况下，买方有权在收到货物之日起的前四个月内，向卖方退回价值相当于原订单 25% 的书籍。当仅订购一本样书时，买方有权将其退回给卖方，但必须在收到之日起不超过四个月内进行。(b) 对于其他书籍（战前出版、古籍及预订版除外），买方有权在收到之日起六（6）个月内，将未售出的任何书籍退回给卖方，退回金额不超过上述书籍名义成本的 10%。买方退回的所有书籍必须状况良好、清洁且页码完整。将货物运回哈尔滨或卖方指定地所产生的所有费用，均由买方账户承担。

(14) 如果买方在不同时间未赎回货物的名义价值达到关平银 300 两，或者买方未按时付款，或在前三季内未赎回价值达关平银 5,000 两的货物，卖方有权单方面终止本协议，买方不得向卖方提出任何索赔。

(15) 如果在一年内，即截至 1933 年 8 月 1 日，买方未从卖方购买第 1 项所述价值达关平银 5,000 两的货物，买方须不迟于 20 天，即 1933 年 8 月 20 日，向卖方支付不足关平银 5,000 两部分的 10% 作为违约金。如果流通额短缺超过关平银 1,000 两，他须支付 20% 而非 10% 的违约金。

(16) 为保证买方履行其在本协议项下的义务，他将签署本协议，并提供令卖方满意的一家外国银行出具的金额为关平银 500 两的保函（期限至 1933 年 12 月 25 日）以及一张金额为关平银 400 两的汇票，该汇票需在半年内兑付。

page_data.en:
(4)

(17) In case any of the goods ordered by the Buyer are not
allowed to pass by the Censor or other authorities, the Buyer
has no claim on the Vendor and the material responsibility
for detained goods is exclusively the Buyer's.

(18) Each party has the right before the expiration of the
term, to discontinue this agreement in case the delivery of
goods in Shanghai is impossible in consequence of import
prohibition by the local authorities or the closure of the
U.S.S.R. and the Chinese borders.

(19) This agreement is made in two copies, Russian and English,
for each of the contracting parties. The Russian text is the
guiding one.
page_data.zh:
(4)

(17) 如果买方订购的任何货物未被审查机构或其他当局准许通过，买方不得向卖方提出索赔，被扣留货物的物质责任完全由买方承担。

(18) 如果因当地当局禁止进口或苏联与中国边境关闭，导致无法在上海交付货物，任何一方均有权在期限届满前终止本协议。

(19) 本协议一式两份，俄文和英文各一份，供缔约各方持有。以俄文本为准。

Dear Sir:-
We have been approached by a British House in Harbin
with a view to us acting as their selling Agents for Soviet
Russian Literature, for which we understand they hold the ex-
clusive rights.

While we would like to enter upon this business, we
thought it preferable to first approach you, by reason of the
possibility that some undesirable literature may probably get
through, although we are given to understand that all books etc,
pass through the censors hands.

We are, as you will see, mainly interested in educat-
ional works, Christian Literature, Medical Works, Childrens books
etc, and obviously do not wish to become entangled in any busi-
ness about which the slightest question may be raised.

Under the circumstances, we shall esteem it a special
favour if you would extend to us your personal opinion as to the
advisability or otherwise of undertaking this Agency, and thank
you in anticipation of that courtesy.

Yours respectfully,
THE KWANG HSUEH PUBLISHING HOUSE
J Burgayeff
